note: Stage-5D.1 four-arm bounded navigation campaign. Exactly two factors vary, crossed: class source (RUNTIME classifier + shipped ambiguity policy vs ORACLE configured-global premise) and max_influence_radius (0.55 m production vs 3.00 m analysis-only, the layer's own declareParameter default and the half-extent of the 6x6 m local costmap). The nav2 params file -- hence MPPI and every critic weight, the planner, the costmap geometry and resolution -- is the SAME UNMODIFIED Stage-4F file in all four arms, so MPPI cannot have been tuned per arm. The window is varied through the layer's own documented runtime parameter; no production YAML is modified. The ORACLE arms are an UPPER-BOUND MEASUREMENT, not a deployable configuration: the node runs the bit-identical Stage-5C.1 global path with class_aware FALSE and has no class input at all, and which premise to configure is chosen outside the robot by the campaign runner from the scenario it is spawning. No ground-truth label reaches the tracker, the costmap layer, the planner or the controller.
layer_percentiles: p95/p99 NOT INSTRUMENTED by the layer; mean and max are reported instead.

A_vs_B.question: Does PERFECT CLASSIFICATION help while the 0.55 m window remains? NO => the classifier is not the primary bottleneck under current policy.

B_vs_D.question: Does EXPANDING THE WINDOW help even with perfect labels? YES => the 0.55 m policy window is suppressing semantic information.
